_about: Side-by-side mode: the numbers for what MORDHAU's character sets down or throws once it exists in Skyrim's world (models: sheets/props.json; keys: sheets/live_input.json). Distances in Skyrim units unless the id says cm; MORDHAU damage values are of its 100 health and go through sheets/progression.json like any MORDHAU-judged hit. source says where each number is from.

rows.meaning: MORDHAU's world gravity, cm/s^2 (Unreal's default)
rows.source: Unreal's default; not read

rows.meaning: Skyrim's stealth eye while MORDHAU is linked: moved this far left of the screen's middle (HUD units, 1280 wide)
... and this far down (HUD units, 720 high)
how near (Skyrim units) the player must stand to the dropped weapon for E to pick it up

Skyrim's fCombatDistance while MORDHAU is linked (Skyrim's own: 141 units = 201 cm, farther than MORDHAU blades reach: enemies swung short of the player). 90 units x the weapon's reach = 129 cm for a sword, 167 cm for a greatsword. Put back when the link ends.
rows.source: measured from the swing log 2026-10-07: swings started from 190-330 cm

rows.meaning: 0 = OFF (play-test note, 2026-10-08). Otherwise: how far (Skyrim units) the player's surroundings are felt for walls, in three directions at chest height
rows.source: own choice

rows.meaning: play-test note, 2026-10-15. 0 = no attack in the mod's session is stopped by MORDHAU's own map (its walls, pillars and props stand where they stand in MORDHAU's arena, not where Skyrim's are): the script sets MORDHAU's bDisableWorldCollision on every attack motion, the player's and the stand-ins'. In the D: test before: 21 enemy swings thrown back (BlockedMotion) 4-6 m from the player, who was not parrying. Skyrim's walls do not stop a blade either while wall_reach and wall_cut are 0 (both off since the play tests of 2026-10-08) - before this, only MORDHAU's map did, at places that had nothing to do with Skyrim's. Script: main.lua PS_no_world_hits (always on; this row is its note).
rows.source: the D: test log, 2026-10-15; MORDHAU's attack motion property found by listing BP_1H_RightStrikeMotion's properties

rows.meaning: 1 = the player's weapon is drawn as the Skyrim weapon that is equipped (Skyrim's own model and textures, placed where MORDHAU's counterpart is); 0 = MORDHAU's model. A weapon picked up in MORDHAU that is not the equipped one's counterpart is always MORDHAU's model.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: 1 = people are Skyrim's own models (their real armour, faces, weapons) moved by MORDHAU's skeleton: whoever is fought - and the player in third person - has the Skyrim skeleton posed from MORDHAU's pose each frame (the bone map of sheets/bone_map.json, run backwards); nobody is drawn as a MORDHAU body. 0 = MORDHAU bodies in MORDHAU armour, as before. A test key overrides it: skyrimbodies=1 in the dev file.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: how far above the spot (Skyrim units) the Skyrim copy of a dropped weapon is set down, to fall the rest by Skyrim's physics (at 12 it started inside the ground and fell through)
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: an enemy that already has a MORDHAU stand-in counts as this much nearer (Skyrim units) when the three nearest fighters are chosen, so stand-ins are not swapped back and forth between enemies at about the same distance
rows.source: stress run 2026-10-08: 12 bandits, a stand-in changed enemy about every 9 seconds (each change re-arms it); 350 on 2026-10-08 (play-testing: characters kept putting weapons and shields away and taking them out)

rows.meaning: 1 = while the player is in something only Skyrim can show (on a mount, sitting / lying / at a workbench, a kill move, swimming, a scripted scene that took the movement or fighting controls away or plays its own animation on the player) Skyrim keeps the player's body and arms, MORDHAU's character stands still and attack inputs are held back; MORDHAU takes the body again half a second after it ends. 0 = MORDHAU's pose always.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: while an ENB is installed (d3d11.dll and enbseries.ini in Skyrim's folder): brightness of everything this plugin draws itself (MORDHAU's first-person body and hands, the weapon in hand, props, gore). The ENB brightens the finished picture; without this the hand and weapon came out far too bright. 0 = unchanged.
rows.source: first-person screenshot with Dawnfire NAT3 ENB, 2026-10-08; set by eye (1.0 was near white in rain, 0.35 near black in fog: 0.6 as a middle; not a real match to the ENB's own lighting)

rows.meaning: 1 = draugr and skeletons that hold a melee weapon get MORDHAU stand-ins like people (they walk on Skyrim's human skeleton); 0 = people only. Animals, giants, dragons and everything that casts stay Skyrim's.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: Skyrim's stamina bar shows MORDHAU's stamina; when Skyrim itself restores more than this many points between two frames (a potion, food, a spell effect), the gain is passed on to MORDHAU's stamina
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08; 15 on 2026-10-08 (at 4, ordinary regeneration was passed on 31 times in one play session)

rows.meaning: an enemy with a blade in its right hand and a spell in its left gets a MORDHAU stand-in like a melee fighter: its blade fights by MORDHAU's rules (parries, feints, MORDHAU's damage), its spells stay Skyrim's - while it casts (and spellsword_cast_linger after), its body is Skyrim's and its stand-in holds its attacks. Pure casters and staff users stay Skyrim's altogether. 0 = anyone with a spell is Skyrim's, as before (an earlier try had such a stand-in point at the ground).
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-18 ('Enemy spell casters who have a weapon in one hand and a spell in another still attack skyrim style')

rows.meaning: spellsword_standin: seconds a cast may stay in one of its starting states (1, 2, 4) before it counts as hung and is interrupted - a Vigilant's Oakflesh stayed in state 1 for good after its attack was broken off, its body stayed Skyrim's and it did nothing
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-20 ('the vigilant tried to cast, changed their mind and just did nothing'); 1.5 a first guess

rows.meaning: spellsword_standin: seconds its body stays Skyrim's after a cast ends (Skyrim's animation lowers the hand), then its stand-in has it again
rows.source: 2026-10-18, a first guess (cast_arm_linger is 0.5 for the player)

rows.meaning: A fought character's Skyrim stamina bar shows its stand-in's MORDHAU stamina (as the player's does), and whatever Skyrim takes off it beyond that - a frost spell, a stamina poison, any mod's effect - its stand-in loses in MORDHAU too, as a share of full: a drained enemy's parries break and cost it its weapon, by MORDHAU's rules; while it is drained, MORDHAU's stamina regeneration of the stand-in waits (as after MORDHAU's own spending: its StaminaRegenDelay after the last drain). Not counted: while it sprints in Skyrim, while Skyrim has its body (yielding, fleeing), and a hit Skyrim blocked. 0 = Skyrim's stamina of fought characters is left alone, as before.
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-18 ('even if other mods drained skyrim stamina it would also drain from Mordhaus bar')

rows.meaning: Skyrim's stamina bar shows MORDHAU's stamina; whatever Skyrim takes off it beyond that - an enemy's frost spell, a stamina poison, any mod's effect - MORDHAU's character loses too, as a share of full, and its stamina does not regenerate meanwhile (as standin_stamina does for enemies). Not counted: the plugin's own spending (a jump's cost), and Skyrim's while sprinting. 0 = only Skyrim's restores are passed on, as before.
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-18 ('Fix Skyrim stamina drains on the player too')

rows.meaning: standin_stamina: the least Skyrim stamina points a fought character must lose between two frames to count as drained (a concentration spell takes a little every frame)
rows.source: 2026-10-18, a first guess

rows.meaning: Skyrim's slows reach a fought character's stand-in: how fast it may move against its normal speed (SpeedMult: a frost spell's slow, or any mod's) scales its MORDHAU movement (MovementSpeedScale), and Skyrim's world time (Slow Time) its whole pace, attacks included (CustomTimeDilation). The player's own MORDHAU character keeps its pace. 0 = stand-ins always move and fight at MORDHAU's speed, as before.
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-18 ('look into slowing enemies down when controlled by Mordhau')

rows.meaning: Skyrim's critical hits count in MORDHAU-judged hits: when the game rolled a critical (its chance from the weapon and perks), the weapon's critical damage raised by the attacker's perks (Bladesman, Bone Breaker, Deep Wounds) multiplies the hit's share of health as it would Skyrim's damage, like the sneak multiplier. Before, it was only in Skyrim's damage, which moves the capped offence: a crit did almost nothing
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-20 ('since backstabs work doesnt that mean crits also work?')

rows.meaning: Power attacks: holding the attack key for Skyrim's own power-attack delay (fInitialPowerAttackDelay) makes the MORDHAU strike a heavy one - a longer windup (heavy_windup), more stamina off whoever parries it (heavy_parry_drain), a larger cost when it misses (heavy_stamina) and Skyrim's power-attack damage (power_attack_damage). An enemy's power attack, as Skyrim's AI chooses it, makes its stand-in's next strike heavy the same way. A tap is a normal strike, sent when the key comes up
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-23 (power attacks, option 1: hold to charge)

rows.meaning: heavy attacks: how much longer the windup is - the telegraph (measured 2026-10-23: MORDHAU takes the weapon's attack table changed just before the attack)
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-23 (power attacks, option 1: hold to charge)

rows.meaning: heavy attacks: the stamina a parry of it costs (MORDHAU's StaminaDrain; less what the parrying weapon absorbs), so two parried heavies can break a parry and disarm
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-23 (power attacks, option 1: hold to charge)

rows.meaning: heavy attacks: what a heavy strike costs its attacker when it misses - MORDHAU charges an attack only then, not when it hits or is blocked (the user, 2026-10-23) - in place of the weapon's own miss cost (never less than it); the player's times Skyrim's power-attack stamina perks (Mod Power Attack Stamina), and with less stamina left the strike stays a normal one. Skyrim's own power-attack spending is not passed on to a stand-in
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-23 (power attacks, option 1: hold to charge)

rows.meaning: heavy attacks: Skyrim's power-attack damage on top of its hit damage, times its power-attack damage perks (Mod Power Attack Damage). An enemy's uses its own power attack's damage multiplier when Skyrim gives one
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-23 (power attacks, option 1: hold to charge)

rows.meaning: A shield MORDHAU knocks away (a shield parry on too little stamina) goes to the ground in Skyrim too, as the Skyrim character's own shield - the player's and a fought enemy's; picked up again the Skyrim way. Before, the Skyrim character kept it and only MORDHAU's disarm sound was heard
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-23 ('Add mirroring shield disarm', 'continue with proper shield disarms')

rows.meaning: Skyrim's slows reach the player: what Skyrim's effects add to the player's SpeedMult (a frost spell's slow, or any mod's; points against a normal 100) slows MORDHAU's character as much (its MaxWalkSpeed), and the pace this mod sets for the Skyrim body keeps them. Before, the base SpeedMult was set to MORDHAU's pace and the speed measuring took the slow for a wrong gain: the slow was lost. Least as standin_slow_least; at most 1.5 (a speed boost)
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-20 ('Slows on the player')

rows.meaning: standin_slow: the slowest a stand-in is made, as a share of its normal speed or pace (MORDHAU's motions are not made for a standstill)
rows.source: 2026-10-18, a first guess

rows.meaning: 1 = with a shield on the arm in Skyrim, MORDHAU's character is handed a shield too (its shield parry); 0 = no shield in MORDHAU (the block button is the plain timed parry)
rows.source: 2026-10-08; switch added when play-testing suspected the shield work of making weapons invisible

rows.meaning: metres around the player (70 Skyrim units a metre) within which everyone in a fight - enemies, allies, archers - gets a MORDHAU stand-in (the nearest standin_limit of them); one that has a stand-in keeps it until it is 2 m beyond, out of the fight, dead or no longer a fighter. Set in the settings menu (Combat page, 5-20 m). Replaces the fixed 700 units for melee and 450 for archers used before
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-16; asked who counts: 'Everyone fighting' (allies included - their stand-ins' MORDHAU brains can go for the player's character, noted)

rows.meaning: how many enemies fight by MORDHAU's rules at once (1 .. Link::kGhosts = 24, the places the link has); the nearest that many. Set in the settings menu (Combat page). MORDHAU's script writes only the places in use, so a lower number costs less
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-16 (with 128 places MORDHAU's pose rate fell from ~200 to 83 a second: a slideshow)

rows.meaning: 1 = a character that has a MORDHAU stand-in does not cower or flee (Skyrim's confidence raised while it is fought)
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: an enemy that draws its weapon keeps Skyrim's own body animation (its unsheathe) until Skyrim has the weapon out, and then for at most this many seconds more while its MORDHAU stand-in is still being handed its weapon; only then is MORDHAU's pose put on it
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08; 3 -> 0.5 on 2026-10-17 (play-test: people took long to draw; MORDHAU had their weapon ready within 0.3-1.3 s)

rows.meaning: 1 = every hit of the player's that Skyrim judges (creatures, anyone without a MORDHAU stand-in) shows MORDHAU's hit marker at the crosshair for a quarter of a second (red when it killed) and plays MORDHAU's own hit sound (its SC_HitIndicator, from MORDHAU); 0 = neither
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: extra reach (Skyrim units) around a creature's own bounds when the player's blade is tested against it; creatures have no MORDHAU stand-in, so the mashup judges these hits itself, against a body shaped from the creature's bounds (long and low for a skeever or wolf)
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: 1 = during the release of a swing, the player's blade breaks breakable things it passes through (spider webs, egg sacs, other activators / movable statics / containers with destruction stages), each once per swing; 0 = off
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: how much damage one swing does to a breakable thing
rows.source: 2026-10-08, a guess: enough for a web in one or two swings

rows.meaning: demonstration scene (dev key demo=1, cell ThroatOfTheWorld01): how far in front of the summit's word wall the player is set down (Skyrim units)
rows.source: a demo for a clip, 2026-10-08; the cell's own arrival point slid off the mountain

rows.meaning: demonstration scene: seconds between the player getting the outfit and the Ebony Warrior being set down
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08

rows.meaning: 1 = a character with a MORDHAU stand-in presses the attack: its Skyrim combat style (shared by all of its kind, until Skyrim is restarted) is set to never fall back, hardly circle and never avoid a stronger opponent; 0 = Skyrim's own behaviour
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-08 (level-1 bandits against the player in Daedric armour)

rows.meaning: 1 again since 2026-10-14 (play-test note): fought people no longer run away or give up; only Skyrim's essential characters still go down on one knee (they cannot die). 1 = a character with a MORDHAU stand-in does not retreat at low health: confidence in its own data is set to 'never flees' and Skyrim's fleeing state is cleared each frame; while Skyrim still has it running away or kneeling, its stand-in holds its attacks. 0 = Skyrim's own behaviour (the stand-in still holds its attacks meanwhile). 0 since 2026-10-12 (play-test note: MORDHAU's AI is not to control people who are yielding or fleeing): Skyrim's own retreat, yield and kneel are left alone; for as long as one lasts the character is Skyrim's - its stand-in holds its attacks, does not move it and does not pose its body.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09: Skyrim takes over and runs away at low health, slowly, while MORDHAU's AI still attacks

rows.meaning: 1 = a head cut off is the Skyrim character's own head and neck wound (Skyrim's decapitation), thrown on MORDHAU's arc (head_throw_out / head_throw_up); nothing of MORDHAU's is put on the body. 0 = MORDHAU's head model and neck piece.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09: make the MORDHAU head invisible and use Skyrim's decapitated head

rows.meaning: how fast (Skyrim units/s) a cut-off Skyrim head is thrown away from the blow - MORDHAU's own launch for a severed head
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09: fly on MORDHAU's arc but with Skyrim's head and neck wound

rows.meaning: ...and upward; Skyrim's physics then carries it on that arc
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09: fly on MORDHAU's arc but with Skyrim's head and neck wound

rows.meaning: 1 = Left Shift is MORDHAU's sprint only: the key is kept from Skyrim, MORDHAU's character sprints while it is held (in any direction MORDHAU allows, its own animation and stamina) and Skyrim's body follows at MORDHAU's speed; 0 = the key starts Skyrim's own sprint (straight ahead only) and MORDHAU copies it
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09

rows.meaning: 1 = a weapon MORDHAU's character throws flies in Skyrim (its MORDHAU model, tumbling unless it is a spear), does MORDHAU's thrown damage for the armour of whom it strikes, leaves the player's hands and inventory and lies where it lands as the real Skyrim item (taken back the normal Skyrim way); 0 = MORDHAU throws but nothing happens in Skyrim
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09

rows.meaning: 0 = the MORDHAU stand-ins of Skyrim's people are mute (MORDHAU's own muffled-voice switch with its volume at 0: no MORDHAU yells, grunts, death screams or voice lines from enemies - they speak only as Skyrim has them speak); the player's MORDHAU voice (battle cry, voice menu, effort and pain) is untouched. 1 = stand-ins speak with MORDHAU's voices as before. Applied by the script (PS_STANDIN_VOICES at its top).
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09

rows.meaning: 1 = a fought character within hybrid_engage_cm of its opponent is moved by MORDHAU's own AI: its stand-in is set free on MORDHAU's floor (closest-enemy override = its opponent) and the Skyrim character is walked after it, each step checked against Skyrim's ground and walls; farther off, and for archers and others that only stand to be hit, Skyrim moves it and the stand-in is held at its place as before. 0 = always held at Skyrim's place. A free stand-in is in MORDHAU's movement mode 5 ('flying': it goes where its brain sends it but does not fall) and its HEIGHT is set every frame to what Skyrim has it at against the player - walking on MORDHAU's uneven arena floor it stood 20-38 cm lower than the player (measured 2026-10-09), so chest-high swings passed over it or counted as head hits.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09 (then the hybrid approach was chosen)

rows.meaning: how near its opponent (cm, MORDHAU's measure) a stand-in is set free; it is held again 150 cm beyond that
rows.source: chosen: about two and a half blade lengths

rows.meaning: units: around a body walked through Skyrim's movement step (hybrid_physics 2), the nearest wall within this distance (8 rays at chest height that pass through characters and loose things) is told to MORDHAU's script with the stand-in's place - its direction in the player's frame and how far - and the script keeps the stand-in from going past it in MORDHAU (its place pushed back out to the wall's line, less standin_wall_margin_cm). 0 = not told
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-17 (item 3 of the improvements: MORDHAU's bots walked into Skyrim's walls - MORDHAU's floor has none - and were set back each time)

rows.meaning: cm: how far short of a told wall's line a stand-in's middle is kept in MORDHAU (about a body's half width)
rows.source: starting value, 2026-10-17

rows.meaning: units: a walked body whose stand-in is farther off than this is not moved towards it at all - the stand-in is set back onto the body (one just given a stand-in was handed over while its bot still stood ~1,450 units away, and the body ran towards it at 721 units/s: D: test 2026-10-17)
units: a walked body this far from its stand-in's place ...
rows.source: starting value, 2026-10-17

rows.meaning: ... for this long: the stand-in is set back onto its body in MORDHAU (it walked where the body cannot follow)
rows.source: starting value, 2026-10-17

rows.meaning: the highest step up or down (Skyrim units) a character is walked over when following its stand-in; a taller change of ground is refused (a ledge, a drop)
rows.source: chosen: a little over Skyrim's own step height

rows.meaning: 1 = while the player draws or puts away a weapon (Skyrim's weapon state: wanting to / doing it), Skyrim has the body like in its other scenes: its own draw and sheathe animations play, in both views, and its own weapon model moves between hand and sheath; MORDHAU's pose returns when the weapon is out (or away). 0 = MORDHAU's pose throughout (its holster motion is a half-second shrug, hardly a draw or a put-away at all).
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09 - so OFF; MORDHAU's own draw and holster motions are to be made visible instead Then, 2026-10-10, Skyrim's own were chosen instead - ON (it works in both views and on a fresh install; MORDHAU's baked draw clips are off).

rows.meaning: 1 = in third person the player's weapon (Skyrim's own model, on the WEAPON node of the Skyrim body) is turned exactly as MORDHAU holds it and set where MORDHAU has it relative to the right hand, every frame - so two-handed grips, the bardiche's other grip and so on look as in MORDHAU; 0 = left where Skyrim's own hand node carries it (a maul sat wrongly in the hands).
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09

rows.meaning: for 0.5 s after a fought character dies, no part of its body moves faster than this (Skyrim units per second; turning limited likewise): a body went limp out of a pose and a place this plugin had set that frame, and Skyrim read the jump as speed - seen in play as people flying off when killed. A head thrown off by a decapitation is left alone. 0 = no limit.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09 (220 chosen: about a brisk fall)

rows.meaning: while a fought character lies limp alive in Skyrim (paralysed, knocked down) and half a second after, no part of its body moves faster than this (Skyrim units per second; turning limited likewise), as death_speed_limit does for the dead: hits on paralysed enemies sent them flying (play test 2026-10-18). 0 = no limit.
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-18 ('paralyze throws the enemy ... or they just fly around'); 220 as death_speed_limit

rows.meaning: a fought character lying limp in Skyrim (paralysed, knocked down) is hit where Skyrim has its body: MORDHAU's blade reaching the line from its head to its feet is a clean hit, as for those without a stand-in. MORDHAU's verdict on its falling stand-in still counts too - either one, once a swing. Its ragdoll in MORDHAU was hard to hit (4 of 11 swings in the play test of 2026-10-18) and not always where Skyrim's body lay. 0 = MORDHAU's verdict alone, as before.
rows.source: the user, 2026-10-18 ('when they lay on the ground ... its still hard to hit them')

rows.meaning: what the player's hit on a creature (anything without a MORDHAU stand-in: wolves, spiders, bears, dragons ...) is multiplied by. 1.25 = a creature falls to a fifth fewer blows: MORDHAU's swings are slower than Skyrim's, and creatures took too long. 1 = as it was.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09

rows.meaning: 1 = in third person the player's own Skyrim shield is what is seen on the arm (the MORDHAU shield chosen by sheets/shield_map.json still decides how it blocks); 0 = MORDHAU's model of that shield is drawn and Skyrim's hidden, as at first. First person still shows MORDHAU's model: Skyrim's shield has to be fitted to MORDHAU's first-person arm by eye.
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-09 (an iron shield was still shown as a targe after the first try)

rows.meaning: play-test note, 2026-10-11. 0: the strip with MORDHAU's health and stamina bars (read from MORDHAU's window) is no longer drawn into Skyrim's picture; Skyrim's own bars are the player's health and stamina. MORDHAU's crosshair with its attack-direction indicator and its voice / emote menu are still shown. 1: as before.

play-test note, 2026-10-11, after an evening of single fixes to how the player's Skyrim body holds weapons (all removed again): place the Skyrim skeleton's hands where MORDHAU's hands are. 1 = while a weapon is out, both hands of the player's own Skyrim body are put where MORDHAU's hands are: each hand's place is MORDHAU's hand measured from the middle between MORDHAU's shoulders, scaled by how long the Skyrim arms are against MORDHAU's, and laid off from the middle between the Skyrim shoulders; upper arm and forearm are turned to reach it (the elbow to the side MORDHAU's is), the hand keeps the turn MORDHAU's pose gave it, the fingers keep the curl Skyrim's animation gave them. The two hands so stand to each other as MORDHAU's do, and the weapon - placed against the right hand as MORDHAU has it - runs through both. 0 = the arms only turned like MORDHAU's bones (hands end where the Skyrim arms' own lengths take them).

see arms_to_mordhau_hands: where a hand's place is still out of the arm's reach (the Skyrim shoulders are not as wide apart as MORDHAU's scaled ones), forearm and hand are set further out along the arm by at most this factor; set outright from the rest skeleton each frame.

play-test note, 2026-10-11: two-handed Skyrim weapons sat too low in the right hand and the iron dagger too high with MORDHAU's placing: MORDHAU's holding point is wherever each MORDHAU model has it. 1 = a SKYRIM weapon model on the player's own body lies on the line MORDHAU's weapon lies on, moved along that line so that its own grip point is in the right fist (the place Skyrim's skeleton has its weapon node in the hand, read from the rest skeleton). MORDHAU weapons (MordhauWeapons.esp) keep MORDHAU's placing. 0 = MORDHAU's placing for all.

player reports, 2026-10-18 (Nexus, and a video): the player's weapon floated beside the hand, in first and third person, with MORDHAU and Skyrim weapons; the people fought were fine. The weapon was set off from the Skyrim wrist as MORDHAU's is from MORDHAU's wrist, and skyrim_weapon_grip_in_fist corrected that only along the weapon - the Skyrim fist does not sit where MORDHAU's does about its wrist, so the grip could come out beside the fist. The fix came from a player who built the mod from its source. 1 = the weapon keeps MORDHAU's line and the right hand is moved onto it: the hand's place (arms_to_mordhau_hands) is moved by how far the Skyrim fist is beside MORDHAU's weapon line, and the weapon is laid in the fist; along the weapon nothing changes. 0 = as before.

with right_hand_onto_weapon, for weapons held in both hands: when MORDHAU's two palms are within 9 cm of one line along the weapon (let go again above 12 cm, so it does not flicker), the left hand is set from the right one as far apart as MORDHAU's hands are, and moved sideways so that the Skyrim left fist lies on the weapon as it is drawn. The left fist's place is the right one's, mirrored - only when the rest skeleton is the same on both sides (logged). 0 = the left hand where arms_to_mordhau_hands puts it.

play-test note, 2026-10-11 (its edge faced backwards; log: the model has its head on its -x side). 1 = a Skyrim weapon model laid along MORDHAU's weapon is turned half round about its own length (players' and enemies'). A sword looks the same both ways. Not yet confirmed by play-testing. play-test note, 2026-10-12 (people on level ground kept starting Skyrim's falling animation): a fought character counts as having yielded - its body is Skyrim's alone, see fought_no_retreat - only after Skyrim has had it out of combat for this long without a break. Skyrim drops and retakes its combat state for moments during a fight; each time the body went to Skyrim's own animation while MORDHAU's AI was still walking it, and a body moved that way is 'falling' to Skyrim. Fleeing and kneeling still count at once. And while a body is Skyrim's alone, MORDHAU's AI does not walk it.

play-test note, 2026-10-12 (bandits' Falx and Ebony Battleaxe had the edge facing back at the holder). 1 = the weapon in the hand of a fought character (a Skyrim body in MORDHAU's movement) is turned the way MORDHAU's stand-in holds its weapon - its length and its edge - as the player's own has been since third_person_weapon_mordhau; it stays at the Skyrim hand's own place. 0 = as before: the weapon simply rides the Skyrim hand, whose grip has the edge the other way round from MORDHAU's.

stand-ins are shown this far in the past (seconds of MORDHAU's own game time): Skyrim keeps MORDHAU's last few reports of each stand-in (pose, weapon, place, heading, each stamped with MORDHAU's clock) and shows the moment this long ago, blended between the two reports around it - even movement however unevenly the reports arrive, and no overshoot (the 'lead' smoothing predicted ahead). Applies to the pose on the Skyrim body, the weapon in its hand, and where a walked body is put. Hits stay MORDHAU's. 0 = the newest report, as before. MORDHAU's clock is set against Skyrim's by the earliest arrival seen (slowly let go)

rows.meaning: play-test note, 2026-10-13 (recorded: with the player walking, the place MORDHAU reports for a free stand-in steps back against its own last step in 11-12% of frames, standing still in 1-4%). MORDHAU's player character walks on the spot: it is let stray up to 5 cm and then set back. Where a free stand-in stands in Skyrim's world, and the shift that keeps it there while the player walks and turns, were reckoned from wherever that character was in the frame - so each stand-in's place took on the same 0-5 cm saw-tooth. Now both are reckoned from the fixed spot. A held stand-in is still placed against the character itself.

play-test note, 2026-10-13 . Measured side by side (tools/heights_compare.py, both games logging the same heights with MORDHAU's game time): the feet of a fought character agree between the two games to about a centimetre, but MORDHAU had its head and hips 9-11 cm HIGHER than Skyrim shows them (within 5 cm only 11-20% of the time). Skyrim draws people in their own sizes - a bandit at 0.98, the player at 1.03 - and in MORDHAU the player and every stand-in are one size. 1 = each stand-in is given its Skyrim character's size against the player's (the two scales divided), so a swing meets the body where it is seen. 0 = all one size, as before.

A free stand-in walks MORDHAU's own ground, which is not Skyrim's: its body is raised or lowered against its capsule so that it stands against the player as its Skyrim character does. The most it is shifted. 60 until 2026-10-13; measured then (tools/heights_compare.py, duels in Riverwood and Whiterun): the shift needed was beyond 60 cm in 4-21% of the samples - the arena's steps and ledges - and never beyond 150; in those moments the stand-in stood up to 75 cm away from where Skyrim showed the fighter. The script's BODY_SHIFT_MOST.

play-test note, 2026-10-13. 1 = the player's kick staggers whoever it reaches that has no MORDHAU stand-in (a wolf, a spider, a draugr beyond the stand-in count ...): Skyrim's own stagger, away from the player. Against a stand-in MORDHAU judges the kick itself, as before. A kick no longer counts as a weapon hit on such an enemy: until now the held weapon's blade was tested during the kick's release and gave a full weapon hit where it happened to pass (seen in the log: 'MORDHAU's blade (BP_KickMotion_C) reached Falmer'). Same day, in play: MORDHAU knows nothing of an enemy without a stand-in, so its kick ran out as a missed one. The plugin now tells the script (request KickLanded) and the script ends the kick motion there, so the next attack can be started at once; MORDHAU's hit marker and hit sound are given as for any hit Skyrim judges.

rows.meaning: Play-test note 2026-10-14: the stand-in, a person at the creature's front, only met swings at the head. Since then the blade is ALSO tested against the creature's whole body (as before the stand-in), and each swing counts once per creature, whichever test counts it first. play-test note, 2026-10-13: 'make it'. 1 = a creature that fights the player (a wolf, a spider, a skeever: anything that is not a person) gets a MORDHAU stand-in that only stands to be hit: passive (never attacks, never parries), held at the creature's front end, as tall against the player as the creature is. MORDHAU itself then judges whether the player's swing or kick lands on it - so a landed kick is a landed kick, a hit can be followed by a combo, a blunt weapon stops in the body - while the creature stays Skyrim's in everything else: its body, its animation, its movement, its own attacks on the player. The damage is still the creature kind (creature_damage_scale of a clean hit); a landed kick gives Skyrim's stagger (kick_stagger_magnitude) and no damage. Stand-in places left over by people go to the nearest such creatures; one without a stand-in (no place left, or taller than creature_standin_tallest) is judged by the blade against its body as before.
